items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 15 at 2:14AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:
A glacier dammed lake outburst from Summit Lake continues on the
Salmon River near Hyder. Water levels on the Salmon River are
expected to continue to rise over the next day or two with an
expected crest sometime on Wednesday or Thursday. It is unknown how
much water will be released from Summit Lake which results in large
uncertainty on crest height and timing.

Potential impact area for this event is the road from Hyder to
Premier, Canada at around mile point 9 along the Salmon River.

Be awar

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 14 at 9:54PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
An east-moving wave will bring with it low temperatures reaching
into the lower 30s, and chances of light freezing rain or drizzle
for the NE Arctic Coast, including locations like Kaktovik and
Point Thomson. Any accumulations are expected to remain minimal,
with conditions improving through the daytime hours on Thursday.
items.areas: Central Beaufort Sea Coast; Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast

items.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 14 at 2:49PM AKDT until July 16 at 12:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Yentna River.

* WHEN...Until noon AKDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water could enter several cabins along the Yentna River near Lake
Creek.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 237 PM AKDT, river gauge reports indicate rises in water
levels from heavy rain across the advisory area. Minor
flooding is expected to begin shortly, especially along the
Yentna River near Lake Creek. Addition
items.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

items.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued July 13 at 4:44PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
ESFAFC

* Glacier Creek in Girdwood

* Early Tuesday morning through Noon Wednesday

Rainfall:

* Around 1.5 inches of rain is expected Monday evening through
Wednesday morning in the Chugach Mountains draining into Glacier
Creek.

Hydrologic Concerns:

* Bankfull conditions can cause water to cover the lowest sections of
Lake Tahoe Road.

* Heavy rain may result in localized ponding in low-lying areas and
locations with poor drainage.

items.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued July 13 at 4:18PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
ESFAFC

* Yentna and Skwentna River drainages

* Monday night through Saturday morning

Rainfall:

* Widespread rainfall of 1.5 to 2.5 inches of rain is expected in
the western Susitna Valley through Wednesday.

Hydrologic Concerns:

* Expect sharp rises on many small streams and rivers. Crests are
expected to occur on Wednesday for most streams and rivers.

* Many lower locations along rivers such as gravel bars and other
spots popular for camping and recreating may become inundated with
water
